name: As found / as left
oneLine: A single unsourced proficiency bar is drawn, then its fill retracts to nothing in front of the reader — and the same claim reassembles beneath it as a compartmented certificate row with a gold-bracketed measured value, a named employer, and a hatched zone at the end marked outside this certificate.
threeSecondRead: The top thing is the bar every portfolio ships, and it is empty — its number had nothing holding it up.
The bottom thing is the replacement: a real figure inside gold jaws, with the place it was taken printed right next to it. That is a calibration card.
The hatched patch at the end is where the certificate stops, and it says so instead of hiding it — which is why the rows above it are worth believing.
form:
A `<figure>` in the header column (max-width 46rem, left-aligned to the lede's old text column), reserved at `min-height: 232px` plus caption. Pure HTML + CSS — zero SVG, zero `<path>`, no measurement, so TC-BENCH-01/02 (`#skills svg path` = 20) are untouched and there is no `getBoundingClientRect` to replay on resize.

Caption first (layer-cake): Source Serif, 1.06rem/1.5, `--white`, first two words carrying the claim — "Nobody can check a percentage. Every row below names where its number was taken."

**Band A — AS FOUND (76px).** Strap, mono 0.6rem/0.16em uppercase `--mist-400`: `AS FOUND · WHAT A PORTFOLIO SHIPS`. Capability label from `capabilities[2].short`, mono 0.78rem `--mist-400`: `Real-time telemetry`. Below it a 360×9px track, 0.5px `--ink-500` border, no fill; inside it a 90%-wide ghost region drawn as 1px **dashed** `--ink-500`, no fill; to its right `90%`, mono 0.8rem `--ink-500` at 0.45 opacity. Under the track: a 0.5px axis with three 4px ticks at 0/50/100%, a printed en-dash `–` beneath each (metrology's "N/A is printed, never blank"), and mono 0.58rem `NO UNIT · NO SOURCE`. Band A never uses `--white` and never uses gold — it sits a full step down the ink ramp.

**The seam.** One 1px `--ink-500` rule, inset 3px at both ends (extension lines don't touch the feature). Right-aligned on it, mono 0.58rem: `17 CAPABILITIES · 13 SOURCES · 20 LINKS · 1 NOT CERTIFIED`, all derived at render.

**Band B — AS LEFT (86px).** Strap `AS LEFT · WHAT THIS PAGE SHIPS`. Same capability label, now `--white`. Then a GD&T feature-control frame: three compartments split by full-height 1px `--ink-500` dividers, square corners, each with its field name above in mono 0.52rem `--mist-400` — `WHAT WAS MEASURED` / `WHERE IT WAS TAKEN` / `WHAT STATE IT IS IN`. Contents: the real `<Caliper state="sourced">` around `10,000+ devices · P95 < 200 ms`; `ANZ Banking Group` (source kind `programme`); `● measured in production`.

**Band C — SCOPE (34px).** A strip occupying the right 34% of the frame, filled with the existing 45° `repeating-linear-gradient` hatch, holding `<Caliper state="open">AWS · GCP</Caliper>` and mono `OUTSIDE THIS CERTIFICATE`; far right, `CV 16b856c0`. The left 66% is deliberately empty.
motion:
One move, four beats, 1,640 ms trigger-to-settled. Trigger: `IntersectionObserver` at `threshold: 0.4`, `disconnect()` on first hit, sets `data-run`; a `[]`-gated `setTimeout(1640)` sets `data-settled`, which applies `animation: none` to every animated child. Base styles are the settled frame; the intro lives inside `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference)` so a missed selector fails static, not animated. Bench's exact two-flag shape.

Beat 1 — the retraction, 0–260 ms. The dashed ghost region is temporarily solid (`background: var(--mist-400)`, 0.5 opacity) and animates `transform: scaleX(1) → scaleX(0)`, `transform-origin: left center`, 260 ms on a new token `--motion-ease-mechanical: cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)` — a measuring instrument does not overshoot, so `--motion-ease-emphasized` is wrong here. Compositor-only. Concurrently, from 60 ms, the `90%` runs `opacity 1 → 0.45` and `letter-spacing 0 → 0.24em` over 180 ms: three glyphs spreading apart and going out, a reading losing its lock rather than being deleted. Track, axis, ticks and printed dashes never move.

Beat 2 — the rule, 260–620 ms. The seam draws left→right, `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0)`, 360 ms, `--motion-ease-standard`. A 1px × 560px box, so the repaint is negligible.

Beat 3 — the inscription, 560–1,240 ms. The three compartments arrive left→right: each `opacity 0→1` + `clip-path: inset(0 100% 0 0) → inset(0)`, 300 ms `--motion-ease-emphasized` (ink arriving, so a soft settle is right), `animation-delay: calc(560ms + var(--i) * 90ms)` with `--i` set inline per the Bench idiom. Inside compartment 0 the caliper's gold jaws fade in over 200 ms at +140 ms — gold is the last ink to land, and it lands only because that figure is sourced.

Beat 4 — the boundary, 1,240–1,560 ms. Band C fades `opacity 0→1`, 320 ms `--motion-ease-standard`, hatch already at full pitch. The hatch itself never animates (paint-heavy repeating gradient). The admitted gap arrives strictly after the evidence.

No loop, no pulse, no scroll-scrubbing, no `will-change` left attached after settle.
states:
**Reduced motion / no-JS.** The settled frame *is* the base stylesheet: empty track with its dashed 90% ghost outline, retracted `90%` at 0.45 opacity, seam ruled, three compartments present with gold jaws closed, hatched scope strip visible. All four beats are present simultaneously as layout, so the argument is identical, not muted. `matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)')` sets `data-run` and `data-settled` synchronously at mount and never starts the observer. The persistent artefact — screenshot, print, VIS-07 baseline, reduced-motion render — never contains a filled bar; the solid fill exists for 260 ms and nowhere else.

**390px.** The figure grid collapses to one column. Band A: track goes `width: 100%; max-width: 15rem`, `90%` drops beneath it, axis keeps three ticks and three printed dashes. Band B: the three compartments restack as three rows; dividers rotate from `border-left` to `border-top`, 1px `--ink-500`; each field name prints inline before its value at 0.52rem mono rather than as a detached header row (direct labels beat a separated key). Band C goes full width. The comparison stays on the vertical axis, which is the correct axis for a before/after on a phone. No horizontal scroll, no shrink-to-fit, no diagram pretending to be readable that isn't.

**Keyboard / screen reader.** Nothing is interactive and nothing enters the tab order, so the section's keyboard contract is unchanged. The `<figure>` is named by its `<figcaption>` via `aria-labelledby`. First in Band A's DOM is a visually-hidden span: "Illustration of the convention this page rejects: an unsourced proficiency bar. It is not a claim about this candidate." Both `<Caliper>` instances carry their existing glosses ("Measured; source given." / "Not measurable; reason given."). No `role="status"` (TC-SKILL-07 safe), no `progress`/`meter`/`role="progressbar"` (TC-SKILL-03 safe). Compartment names at `--mist-400` on `--ink-900` clear AA comfortably. The displaced lede is retained verbatim in `skills.ts` and rendered as a visually-hidden long description on the figure, so no sentence leaves the page.
coherence:
It extends three devices the site already owns and adds no new vocabulary. The `<Caliper>` component is used as a component, in two of its three taught states — `sourced` around the ANZ figure, `open` around AWS · GCP — so the reader spends their one unit of learning budget on the mark the site already asks them to learn, not a fourth one. The 45° hatch is the existing `repeating-linear-gradient` from `Caliper.module.css`, used for exactly its existing meaning: inside this boundary, nothing was certified. The `--i` inline stagger, the `IntersectionObserver` + `drawn`/`settled` two-flag pattern, and "the animation is never the source of truth for the resting style" all come straight from `Bench.tsx`.

It deliberately avoids every device another section spends: no dial, bezel, radial gauge or index-at-twelve (About/Compass); no wires, rails, node-link graph or hover-dimming (the Bench directly below it); no box-and-arrow flow, no literal drawn caliper illustration (Vitrine's `Drawings.tsx`); no shader, no canvas — TC-CINE-04 requires zero `<canvas>` in `#skills` under reduced motion. The one genuine tension is Experience's horizontal duration bars; this bar is answered by being explicitly axis-less and then destroyed, which is the opposite claim, but it is the concept's honest weak point.

Gold appears in exactly one place in the whole figure: the two caliper jaws around `10,000+ devices · P95 < 200 ms`, whose source `ANZ Banking Group` is printed 40px to its right and is verifiable by ringing the employer. It is a terminator, never a path — no gold axis, no gold track, no gold fill, no gold on the strap or the hatch. Band A contains no gold at all, which is the lesson: the bar has nothing to be gold about. Every colour is `var(--*)`, so the static MONO audit and the computed-style MONO-04 sweep both pass, and MONO-05 (gold must render in `#skills`) is reinforced rather than threatened.

Placement: it sits between `<header>` and `<Bench>` and **absorbs the lede** — `.lede` is removed from the header, its second sentence becomes the `<figcaption>`, its first sentence survives as the figure's visually-hidden description. Nothing else is displaced.
risks: The mid-animation frame briefly shows 'Real-time telemetry 90%' as a filled bar. A 260 ms screen capture could be quoted as his self-rating. Mitigated four ways (settled frame has no fill, AS FOUND strap, visually-hidden disclaimer, Band A held a full step down the ink ramp with no white and no gold) but not eliminated.

It reuses horizontal-bar language that Experience already spends on 16-year duration bars. The defence — this bar has no axis and is destroyed — is real but requires the reader to notice the absent unit. A hostile reviewer can fairly call it a repeat.

Three bands plus caption adds roughly 300px to the pre-Bench header zone, pushing the Bench below the fold on a 900px-tall laptop. The section already asks for a lot of vertical scroll before its main diagram.
The whole figure rests on twelve words of Source Serif. If the caption is vague, the drawing becomes a puzzle and the concept is worse than the prose lede it replaced.
Animating `letter-spacing` on the retracting figure repaints. It is three glyphs for 180 ms, which is fine, but an implementer who applies the same trick to a longer run will hit real jank.

Deleting the lede risks losing the word 'certificate' for prose readers. If the visually-hidden long description is dropped as 'redundant' in a later cleanup, the metaphor's only verbal anchor leaves the page.

`clip-path` is a paint property, used here on three small boxes; on a slow device with a fresh font swap mid-beat the compartments could stutter. Fixed-size boxes and `contain: layout paint` on the figure are required, not optional.
whyBest:
It is the only concept that puts the rejected object on screen. Every alternative — a vernier, a guard band, a traceability ladder, an annotated specimen row — is a beautiful drawing that merely *is not* a proficiency bar. But the visitor arrives with a template in mind, and a template is displaced by a controlled counterexample, not by an assertion. National Geographic teaches chart deception by putting the truncated axis beside the honest one with the data held constant; this does exactly that, holding the capability label constant across both registers so the only variable is whether the number has anything under it.

It answers all three of the visitor's questions in one still frame, with no prose. *What is this?* — the three named compartments spell out a certificate's fields without a legend. *What does it mean here?* — a real capability, a real precise figure, a real employer you can ring. *Why am I not seeing bars?* — because an empty track with `NO UNIT · NO SOURCE` printed under it is sitting directly above the row that replaced it.

It is also the cheapest and safest thing on the shortlist to build. No SVG means no `<path>`, so TC-BENCH-01 and TC-BENCH-02 keep passing unmodified — every other candidate requires re-scoping two tests before a line of the visual is written. No layout measurement means no `ResizeObserver`, no double-rAF settle, no replay-on-resize, no CLS. Two fill-free boxes and a `transform: scaleX()` mean the single most expensive moment is compositor-only. It reuses the Caliper component rather than redrawing it, so the mark cannot drift.

And the settled frame is stronger than the animation, which is the test the motion research sets: screenshot it and the argument is fully present — empty track, ruled seam, bracketed sourced value, hatched boundary. The animation only tells you *how* the empty track got empty. That is exactly the right division of labour for a section whose own code comment insists it should be flat, dense and silent.
